title: Second Shot Metering Change for the Cargo Compartment Extinguishing Distribution
abstract: Cancelled proposal to re-meter the cargo compartment extinguishing second shot on long-fuselage aircraft, dropped after analysis showed the existing distribution already met the extended suppression requirement without hardware change.

sections.reason: The extended suppression time required for long-range operation on the longest fuselage variant was expected to need a re-metered second shot, because the original distribution had been sized for a shorter compartment and a shorter certification duration. Two operators planning transatlantic operation asked for a position, and a modification was opened to change the metering orifice sizes and the manifold branch balance so that the aft compartment received a larger share of the second shot.
sections.description: The proposal replaced the metering restrictor HAD420992-96 with a set of three orifices sized per branch, changed the transmitter D2620124332034 to one with a wider calibrated range, and re-balanced the manifold so that the aft branch received sixty per cent of the second shot instead of fifty. The accumulator D2620126509607 would have been retained. Work would have been in zones 151 and 182 with the bulk cargo lining removed, and the actuator at FIN 598WD and the manifold at FIN 758WF would have been disturbed. The distribution layout is on drawing D26201226724.
sections.effects: The proposal would have added 2.3 kilograms in the aft lower fuselage with no electrical effect. During the analysis, full-scale discharge testing on a representative compartment showed that the existing distribution already achieved the required concentration for the extended duration on the long fuselage variant, with margin, because the compartment leakage rate assumed in the original sizing had been conservative. The change would therefore have delivered no benefit while introducing a new certification test campaign and a fleet-wide re-metering exercise.
sections.embodiment_note: No embodiment. The modification was cancelled in September 2024 once the discharge test results were available. The operators who raised the request were given the test evidence and the extended suppression time was granted against the existing configuration.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft lower fuselage, CG shift 0.03 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: None; cancelled before any line activity
